utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good afternoon to the Prosecution, to Mr. Seselj, and to everyone assisting us in this case. Let's deal with a number of housekeeping matters before we have the witness brought in. First of all, let me turn to the Prosecution. How much time have you planned for the examination-in-chief of the following witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we have been granted three hours for the presentation of the evidence of the witness, but I think we can do with less than that. Maybe two and a half hours or maybe even less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I am asking the question because of the following: If things happen that way, we will sit tomorrow, but not on Thursday, because Witness VS-32 will not be coming. And I understand, Mr. Seselj, that you were not informed that VS-32 was not coming.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I said that ten minutes ago to the representative of the Registry, and I think that they should inform me at least yesterday, because this other witness was the first one on the list here today; and all the papers I brought in today were for that witness, who's not going to come. I think that this is improper conduct on the part of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It may very well be that the Prosecutor forgot to notify you. I'm not sure. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the circumstances under which the witness in question was supposed to come, we have not been aware of whether he was going to appear or not, so I'm afraid there is a -- it has been difficult for everyone to know whether or not the witness would actually be here today or not. It's unfortunate if the accused had been under the impression that it would be 32. The witness we have been sure about would be -- was 16. And as we have two days -- well, we have three days available this week, I'm sure the accused will be able to prepare his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, despite all this, you'll be conducting the cross-examination of the next witness tomorrow. You'll have the opportunity to bring your documents tomorrow. Secondly, I investigated the matter of telephone communications. We made some inquiries with the Registry, and that's what we found out. Following the explanations given to us by the Registry, you had a telephone line with your associates, and you had been informed that this telephone line would be monitored, but they were unable to monitor that telephone line. It appeared to be completely impossible, technically speaking. That's why they told you -- they informed you that you were to make phone calls from the phone booth available to everyone at the detention centre. Well, I suppose that the Registrar could have set up a different system, but he has not done so. You were right, indeed, to say that this telephone line was cut. Yes, that indeed happened. But why? Because they could not monitor this particular telephone line. I believe that at the moment, they are looking for another telephone or another room to make things easier and where they can monitor you. So now I understand, because at the time when you told us about this, I didn't understand why they had cut the telephone line. And the reason is a very technical and simple one. They can't monitor that telephone line. Now, when it comes to the actual reason why, technically speaking, they can't monitor that line, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, now I wonder whether you are announcing a continuation of this monitoring to me, because the Registrar's decision said that that would be within the period of 30 days, and that expires tomorrow. I haven't received a new decision from the Registrar yet, but I guess it's the standard mechanism like when they banned all my telephone conversations with my family, friends, everybody, and visits by my family, friends, everybody, month by month. It went on for seven months. I'm not going to contact my associates under those conditions, anyway. I call them almost every today, but we talk only about political questions through this regular telephone used by all the convicts. I do not want to discuss anything related to this case over a telephone that is monitored. I will not. So my communication with my associates has been completely cut off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're right, this period of 30 days is going to end tomorrow. I have no idea what the Registrar will decide. It's up to him to decide what's to be done. But you have referred the matter to the Trial Chamber, and the Trial Chamber will rule on this once our deliberations are over. If the Registrar decides to monitor your telephone communications again, well, I don't know, that's a possibility. I can't tell you anything about this. The following witness will be a protected witness. We need to draw down the blinds and to move into closed session. Madam Registrar, closed session, please, and please draw down the blinds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 29th day of October, 2008, at 2.15 p.m. 22 23 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
